title: The template, made from what surya proved
note: device.toml with every section devlab reads (connection, provision, flash, health) and what to change; tests/health for a phone's own checks; tests/results for its reports; AGENTS.md conventions; CI for its scripts; its mark. Every tool is devlab's, reading the manifest - nothing is copied.

title: device.toml read off a running phone
note: devlab reads a running phone (compatible, sound cards, signal processors, inputs) and proposes its device.toml, [health] included - the onboarding step of the device-template design (linux-phone-oco/docs backlog device-template, point 6).

title: A second phone through the template
note: The proof that surya is not the mould: a second postmarketOS phone's lab made by Use this template, reaching healthy with only its device.toml filled.

title: surya-lab re-based onto the template
note: surya-lab keeps scripts the template no longer needs (lib/phone.sh, tests/run.sh, tests/to-docs.sh, tests/automatic/checks.sh, flash/, provision/provision.sh): each one retires once devlab does its work, its reasons carried first (Chesterton's fence). Done when surya-lab holds only data a template-made lab holds.

title: The lab's USB wake lock, carried by devlab
note: Every lab phone on USB needs devlab-usb-awake (a suspend attempt drops the link); surya carries it as its own overlay. It belongs to devlab, written at flash for any phone.
